children: The Navratna power producer also aims to increase mining capacity to 104.35 MTPA and renewable energy capacity to more than 10 GW by 2030
State-owned NLC India has raised Rs 500 crore through the issuance of commercial papers, as the power producer advances its capacity expansion plans and long-term mining and renewable energy targets.

The company issued and allotted 10,000 commercial papers with a face value of Rs 5 lakh each on 22 September, according to a filing with the BSE. Commercial papers are short-term, unsecured debt instruments used by companies to raise funds.

NLC India, a Navratna public-sector enterprise under the Ministry of Coal, currently has an installed power-generation capacity of 8,405 MW and a mining capacity of 59.1 million tonnes per annum (MTPA). The company plans to invest Rs 1.25 lakh crore by 2030 to expand its capacity.

NLC India aims to increase its total mining capacity to 104.35 MTPA by 2030 and 115.85 MTPA by 2047. The company said the expansion is intended to support India’s electricity requirements and reduce dependence on imported coal.
Alongside its mining operations, the company is working to modernise its power-generation portfolio through responsible mining practices and investments in clean energy.

NLC India Renewables (NIRL), the company’s green-energy subsidiary, is leading its renewable energy expansion. NLC India plans to increase its operational renewable energy capacity from 1.8 GW currently to more than 10 GW by 2030 and 32.7 GW by 2047.
The company expects the expansion to increase clean energy’s share of its overall generation mix to 50 per cent ahead of its previously scheduled target.
